strings.title: The Darkened Lighthouse
strings.hint: A ship sank because the lighthouse went dark at the wrong moment… who stood to profit from its wreck? Trace the emergency generator key.
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: the greedy retired lighthouse keeper, Wadie Salama… no, his smuggling partner: salvage dealer Ghaleb Morsi.

The truth: Ghaleb Morsi arranged to extinguish the lighthouse on the night a cargo ship carrying a valuable container passed, making it strike the rocks so his company could buy the wreck and cargo cheaply. He bribed the current keeper to leave the backup generator disabled, but the keeper refused at the last moment. Ghaleb strangled him, extinguished the light himself, and stole the generator key.

The emergency generator key in his boat, a salvage purchase contract dated a day before the sinking, and a transfer to the murdered keeper exposing the attempted bribe proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: On a stormy night, the Ras Al-Sokhour lighthouse went dark for the first time in forty years. A cargo ship struck the rocks and its cargo sank. When the coast guard climbed to the lighthouse, they found its keeper strangled beside the backup generator, its ignition key missing. The darkness was not fate. It was a double crime: murder and a deliberate sinking.

strings.scene.address: Ras Al-Sokhour lighthouse — upper room and generator chamber
strings.scene.intro: A long spiral staircase leads to an unlit lamp at the top. The backup generator works, but its ignition key is missing and the keeper lies beside it. There is no sign of forced entry. The keeper welcomed his visitor.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The lighthouse summit and the raging sea
strings.scene.notes[0]: The generator works, but its key is missing
strings.scene.notes[1]: No forced entry — the keeper knew his visitor
strings.scene.notes[2]: The ship carried a high-value container
strings.scene.notes[3]: A salvage purchase contract dated before the sinking
strings.evidence[0].title: The Missing Generator Key
strings.evidence[0].desc: The emergency generator's ignition key. Without it, the lighthouse stays dark. It was found in Ghaleb's possession.
strings.evidence[1].title: Salvage Purchase Contract
strings.evidence[1].desc: A contract to buy the sunken ship's cargo cheaply, dated a full day before the sinking.
strings.evidence[2].title: The Bribe Transfer
strings.evidence[2].desc: A large sum was transferred to the keeper by Ghaleb a week earlier, followed by a request for its return a day before the incident.
strings.evidence[3].title: Ship Cargo Manifest
strings.evidence[3].desc: A container of expensive medical equipment was aboard, the real target of the sinking.
strings.evidence[4].title: Boat Rope Traces
strings.evidence[4].desc: A small boat moored below the lighthouse that night. The rope type matches boats used in the salvage trade.
strings.suspects[0].name: Nouh, the Ship's Captain
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was battling the waves to save my ship. I barely survived."
strings.suspects[0].statement: Forty years at sea and I'd never lost a ship. The lighthouse suddenly went dark. If it had been working, I would have avoided the rocks. Whoever put it out sank my ship and my crew. Look for who profited from the wreck, not who lost the vessel.
strings.suspects[1].name: Rami, the Keeper's Son
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I was fishing far out at sea with my colleagues."
strings.suspects[1].statement: My father devoted his life to this lighthouse. In his last days he was anxious and argued on the phone with a man I didn't know. I warned him about Ghaleb Morsi, but he said, "I've dealt with it." Whoever killed him stole my father from me. Help me find out who.
strings.suspects[2].name: Ghaleb Morsi
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I was home on the night of the storm. The weather made sailing impossible."
strings.suspects[2].statement: The salvage trade is legal and honorable. I buy what sinks; I don't sink it. My contracts are ordinary business papers. The keeper was an old friend. If I sent him money, it was to help a sick friend. The sea swallows ships without anyone's help.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Coast Guard Officer
strings.witnesses[0].statement: We found the generator in perfect working order. If started, it would have lit the lighthouse within seconds. Only the key was missing, as though someone wanted it to stay dark.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Nearby Fisherman
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I saw a small boat moor below the lighthouse before the light went out, then speed away after the collision. It wasn't a fishing boat. It was moving without lights.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Ghaleb's Accountant
strings.witnesses[2].statement: I resigned because I saw contracts dated before the sinkings occurred. I asked once and was told: "Good prediction is the foundation of business." I didn't believe it.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Sinking Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: A ship was reported to have struck rocks after the lighthouse went dark. The coast guard responded.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Autopsy report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Forceful manual strangulation; death occurred minutes before the collision. Signs of resistance on the keeper's hands.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Generator Examination
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: The generator is in excellent condition. There was no fault; the light was deliberately disabled by removing the key.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Boat Rope Analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: Rope fibers on the rocks match ropes used on salvage boats.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Ship Cargo Record
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: A container of high-value medical equipment. Ghaleb bought it from the "wreck" for a tenth of its price.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: The Keeper's Account Statement
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: A large transfer from Ghaleb a week earlier, with urgent messages demanding its return a day before the incident.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Boat Seizure Record
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: Ghaleb's boat was seized with the missing generator key and remnants of rescue equipment from the container aboard.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Recovered Messages
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Ghaleb's messages to the keeper: "Leave the generator alone on Thursday night and take the rest." The keeper's final reply: "I can't… I'll report it." Hours later, he was dead.
strings.reports[0].title: Deliberate Sinking Report
strings.reports[0].author: Coast guard
strings.reports[0].body: The lighthouse was disabled by removing the key at precisely the time the ship passed, a planned operation to drive it onto the rocks.
strings.reports[1].title: Beneficiary Report
strings.reports[1].author: Financial investigation unit
strings.reports[1].body: The contract dated in advance and the purchase of the wreck at a bargain price narrow the motive to the salvage dealer.
strings.notes[0].text: Working generator + missing key = deliberate blackout
strings.notes[1].text: A purchase contract a day before the sinking. Who can see the future?
